import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I've submitted a fix plan for the sase CI failure and it's waiting for your approval. No repo files have been changed yet.

**What's failing:** Master Gate run #3785, for commit `1a468da` ("feat(memory): add audited roster web read…"), failed in shard `test (6)`. The two failing tests check that the saved snapshot of the CLI's completion spec still matches the actual command definitions:
- `tests/completion/test_snapshot.py::test_checked_in_snapshot_has_no_drift`
- `tests/completion/test_snapshot.py::test_current_structural_view_matches_checked_in_snapshot`

Both also fail locally at the current tip (`8e6818d`). The two newer commits still have the problem, so their Master Gate runs, still in progress when I checked, will fail the same way.

**Root cause:** `1a468da` added a new `-a/--all-strands` flag to `sase memory read` and `sase memory show` and changed their help text. It didn't regenerate `tests/completion/snapshots/cli_spec.json`. Comparing the snapshot with the live CLI shows only those two commands changed.

The same commit's CLI reference docs, which are generated from the same command definitions, were updated correctly because `just fix` regenerates them. The completion snapshot is only regenerated by hand with `just sync-completion-spec`, and neither `just fix` nor `just lint` runs it. That's why this has slipped through before (`2e04694766`, plus earlier resyncs noted in the flake baseline).

**The plan (small):**
1. Run `just sync-completion-spec` to regenerate the snapshot, and confirm the change covers only `memory read` and `memory show`.
2. Your choice, `autosync`, defaulting to yes: copy what the Footprint catalog already does.
   - `just fix` regenerates the snapshot.
   - A new `sync-completion-spec-check` step in `just lint` fails if it's out of date. It adds about 1 second per run.
   - The Justfile contract tests are updated to match.

   Choosing `snapshot_only` does just step 1.
3. Verify with the completion and Justfile tests, then `just fix` and `just check`, and finally confirm the next Master Gate run goes green.

**Separate issue:** the `sase` on your PATH is older than this workspace and rejects `sase memory read roster:decisions`, so I used the workspace's own copy. Global reinstalls are human-only, so this will keep happening until you reinstall it.

`actstat` also shows failures in other repos (dotfiles, bob-cli, sase-core, sase-github, bobs-org.github.io). I left those out because you asked about the sase repo.
